newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi says EMU rows reveal Italy budget lies.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi says EMU rows reveal Italy budget lies.

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi said on Tuesday rows with France and Spain over Italy's ability to qualify for European monetary union revealed all the "lies" of the government's 1997 budget.

"The truth now is plain to everyone in the public opinion of our European partners -- with this budget, based solely on new taxes and no public spending cuts, Italy runs serious risks of not making it into Europe," he said in a statement.

French President Jacques Chirac rowed back from a diplomatic storm sparked by a comment earlier on Tuesday that Italy might not have its finances in order to become a founder member of a single currency planned for launch in 1999.
He later said he "ardently hoped" Italy would succeed.

Italy's centre-left government unveiled a 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) deficit-cutting budget last week -- nearly twice as big as forecast -- after realising that Spain would not join it in any attempt to have the single currency criteria softened.

Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said in an interview on Monday that Madrid was determined to be there at the start, prompting Italian Prime Minister Prodi to say that the issue had never arisen and Italy, too, was determined to make the grade.

"The remarks by the French president and Spanish prime minister have blown apart in less than 24 hours the lies of the Prodi government," said Berlusconi, who leads the main opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance.

Berlusconi, who has promised firm parliamentary resistance to the budget and says he will unveil a counter-package on Thursday, said Italy now had to prove its determination to its European partners with concrete cuts.
The budget includes a one-off "Euro-tax" and spending cuts worth $25 trillion lire but opposition and business leaders slammed Prodi for not reducing pensions and welfare provisions.

"The opposition will fight together, with all its forces, to prevent this budget built on recession and against development from worsening the problem of unemployment and leading the economy of this country into disaster," Berlusconi said.
